title: 2D Shapes: Circles, Triangles, Rectangles and Squares
standard_text: K.6A identify two-dimensional shapes, including circles, triangles, rectangles, and squares as special rectangles; K.6D identify attributes of two-dimensional shapes using informal and formal geometric language interchangeably; K.6E classify and sort a variety of regular and irregular two- and three-dimensional figures regardless of orientation or size; K.6F create two-dimensional shapes using a variety of materials and drawings
meta_desc: Free kindergarten 2D shape worksheets for Texas TEKS K.6A, K.6D, K.6E and K.6F: circles, triangles, rectangles and squares, sides and corners, and making shapes. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Count the sides and corners to name a shape.
key_sub: A square is a special rectangle.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Circle: round, no sides, no corners.
  • Triangle: 3 sides, 3 corners.
  • Rectangle: 4 sides, 4 square corners. A square is a rectangle with 4 equal sides.
  • Size, color and turning do not change a shape's name.

Examples

Example

3 sides and 3 corners

count the sides

Answer: triangle

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Naming a shape by color or sizeA small red triangle is still a triangle.
Thinking a turned square is not a squareTurning does not change the shape.
Counting a corner twiceStart at one corner and go around.
